task_description: Re-integrate the human-governance layer (superseded PR #24 / origin/feat/admin-governance-layer, now 21 commits behind main and non-mergeable) onto current main, then extend it to deliver the user's asks: (1) a reset-to-onboarding control that puts an account's entrypoint Bot 'Chief' back through its first-conversation brief and re-fires the greeting without destroying audit/evidence; (2) an admin action to ARCHIVE (revoke/snapshot, never hard-delete) a bot's memory/workspace data, preserving the append-only evidence trail; (3) a full-admin account admin@amazai.co seeded as an ACTIVE Owner in the governance Directory via a deploy-time bootstrap script + the OWNER_SUBJECTS/OWNER_EMAILS allowlist, with NO password literal anywhere in the repo (password set at first login in Auth0 / injected out-of-band); and a SEPARATE /admin web surface (distinct route group outside the chat Shell, no bot composer) consuming the /admin/* routes with the blueprint's typed-confirm+reason destructive-action UX. Plus a re-assessment of governance on the changed repo (org chart, cost metering, memory scopes, provisioning, streaming) with genuinely-needed gaps folded in or recorded as follow-ups. First mergeable slice: FEAT-001..004. Honest single-tenant with a documented seam is acceptable for this slice (the user acknowledged single-tenancy); true multi-tenant read path is a deferred follow-up. This branch SUPERSEDES PR #24.

verification.summary: All four features complete and committed source-only (7fc979f, 21cbcf8, c958b9d, a520350, plus review-fix commits dbe3cae and 58fd6e7). Final pass after the semantic-review loop: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -> 1284 passed / 3 failed (the 3 are the documented PRE-EXISTING tests/test_gaps_api.py failures from moto/boto3 drift, unchanged from the 992/3 clean-main baseline; ~292 new tests all pass). cd infra && npx cdk synth -> exit 0. cd web && npm run build -> exit 0, dist/index.html present, grep -c demoApi dist/assets/*.js == 0 (no demo leak). cd web && npm test (Node 22) -> 146 passed. No Dockerfile drives this feature, so docker_build is skipped. Test quality: the admin-api suite is behavioural, not static -- the RBAC-negative tests for reset-onboarding and archive-memory assert 403 AND that no state change occurred AND that NO admin-audit row was written (the gate fires before any write); the suspended-admin tests mutate the caller's own MEMBER# row to SUSPENDED and prove the next action fails closed via guard_principal; the frozen-org tests write a real killswitch row and prove the action is blocked; archive proves the memory row SURVIVES (revoked, is_visible->False) while evidence/agent-AUDIT rows are byte-identical before/after; reset proves is_brief(systemPrompt)==True is restored and the greeting re-seeded while agent-audit rows are untouched; the no-password guard test assembles the forbidden literal from fragments so neither it nor its .pyc is a false offender, and walks the tracked source asserting the literal appears nowhere. All would fail if the enforcement were reverted. Working tree left clean apart from the untracked .agents/ plan dir; __pycache__/*.pyc churn reverted so commits are source-only.

new_gaps_found: COST METERING has no org-wide budget cap wired to the kill switch: cost.py enforces PER-AGENT budgets (budget_for_agent, on_ceiling hard_stop/warn) but there is no org/per-user aggregate cap or a 'stop all runs' tie between a budget breach and govern's kill switch. This is a genuine newly-relevant governance gap (blueprint MANAGE_PAYMENT/SEE_ALL_USAGE + kill switch). RECORDED AS FOLLOW-UP -- the kill switch built here is the enforcement primitive an org-budget-cap would trigger; wiring an aggregate cap to it is a clean next slice, not required for this mergeable slice.

ORG REPORTING CHART (org.py) is explicitly 'organization, not authority' and enforces no capability, so it introduces NO authority-confusion enforcement gap. An ADMIN read-view of the chart is a reasonable console addition but not a governance necessity -- FOLLOW-UP.

MEMORY proposals + CONNECTOR revokes admin-visibility: memory shared_user proposals go through the approval gate and connector grants are per-agent, but neither surfaces in an ADMIN audit/visibility view today. The admin audit trail + /admin/audit built here is the envelope; adding connector.revoked_by_admin and memory-proposal visibility routes (the branch already reserved the audit actions) is a FOLLOW-UP once the base admin surface lands.
STREAMING (stream.py) added a live channel but no new principal-authorization gap beyond what identity/ownerId already enforce -- no action needed this slice.
deferred_followups_from_prior_task: Real multi-tenant read path (org-owned rows + subject->org lookup) remains the big deferred item; the user explicitly accepted single-tenant for now, so honest single-tenant with a documented seam is retained. load_membership + the bootstrap script both document the seam.

Blueprint MVP items still not built: org ask-first policies + approval queue, usage/hard-budget-cap admin routes wired to the kill switch, impersonation break-glass route (IMPERSONATE + impersonation.started/ended audit actions already reserved), connector-revoke-by-admin route.

v1.5+: workspaces/hard isolation (the (subject,role,scope,scope_id) tuple is already modelled), network allowlists, SIEM/OTel export (admin-audit envelope is versioned for it), routine governance, chargeback tags, secret scanning, true origin-isolated admin app (this slice uses a distinct in-app route group instead).
